title: TMC does
*none of the three*
yet
slides.notes: The deck's one sentence: winners charge a real price, say one checkable thing, and let the pack prove it. TMC does none of the three yet.

slides.title: The answer first

rows.label: Winners hold one price. TMC's Black shows two list prices and sells from Rs 180 to Rs 740 (I).
Winners name a number, a percentage or a guarantee. TMC is one of five persona brands, and its page opens with the discount.
Winning packs prove the claim or break the black shelf. Rivals offer a trial at Rs 59 to 149. No TMC mini was found.
Price level does not explain who sells more. Brand power shows in how little a brand discounts, not in how high it lists.

title: No price
*is real*
to the buyer
slides.sub: TMC'S PRICE PROBLEM IS COHERENCE, NOT LEVEL — FIX IT BEFORE ANY PRICE INCREASE
slides.notes: Pause here. One bottle with two list prices and selling prices from Rs 180 to Rs 740 teaches the buyer that no price is real. Confirm on the live pages, then fix it before any price increase: one list price and one selling price on every channel.

slides.title: Price does not predict sales; *deep discounts* cost margin

rows.label: Price does not predict sales
rows.sub: Brands whose hero perfume sells at Rs 449 to 799 have company sales of $9M to $54M. The cheapest (Bella Vita) is the largest; the dearest at full price (Bombay Shaving) grows fastest (Chapter A §2).

rows.label: Discount depth runs opposite to margin
rows.sub: The three brands near list all earn 25 to 37% (Reginald 25%, Muuchstac 37%, Gillette 31%); TMC, the deepest discounter, loses money. Bella Vita is the exception: its fixed discount is the brand idea.

rows.label: Brand power shows as engagement and ratings, not followers
rows.sub: TMC and Ustraa have audiences of similar size to rivals and almost no engagement. Beardo's engagement is about 200 times TMC's (I).

slides.notes: Margins and the Bombay Shaving growth figure: Chapter A §2 (state the margin type and year when asked). TMC's own margin figure is not on the slide.

slides.title: Fix price *coherence* first, then pick one of two positions

rows.label: A premium is paid for a specific result, never for a general identity

rows.label: TMC's price problem is coherence, not level

rows.sub: A fixed, honest price in the core band with a checkable claim, or a two-times premium on one named result. Every persona brand already stands in the struck-through middle.

slides.title: A working message carries *a checkable number*; TMC's page offers none

sections.head: WORKS
items: A claim with a number the buyer can verify — it replaces trust with a test
One message per page — the buyer decides in seconds
A guarantee — it moves the risk to the seller
A character taken to the extreme and paired with a result claim — memorable and still checkable
Naming the problem in the product title — it matches what men type into search

sections.head: DOES NOT WORK
items: “Premium”, “long lasting”, “signature” — every rival says it; it cannot be checked
A premium headline above a clearance banner — the second message cancels the first
A certificate nobody understands — it reassures without proving
A mild character — describes no one in particular
Naming the range or the mood — nobody searches for it

slides.notes: Companion document, section 2.5.

sections.head: WORKS
items: A pack that proves the claim — Fogg
Breaking the category colour — CODE white; Bombay Shaving blue, with offline growth

sections.head: DOES NOT WORK
items: A pack that only signals “premium” — sameness of black packs across the persona group
Dark, low-contrast or gold-foil packs on quick commerce — they “lose almost all contrast” on a white page (a design agency's view)
Several claims and badges on the front — unreadable at 200 pixels
Trial only through a gift box — Rs 499 to 599 against Rs 149 for a rival's pocket size
Sample vials and pumps that leak — Beardo reviews; one bad unit produces a one-star review

slides.notes: Two cautions: the quick commerce points come from one design agency (Confetti), and no source measures the effect of packaging on sales except Bombay Shaving's offline move and Engage's pocket pack. Mintel citing FICCI 2015, Storyboard18 (F).

slides.title: Test five changes to TMC's packs: *fix the spray, add a mini* (1 of 2)

rows.label: Fix the content and the spray first
rows.sub: Black's pack promises quality and the content varies from bottle to bottle.

rows.label: Add an entry pack under Rs 200
rows.sub: The same product in a smaller size, not a different format.

rows.label: Put one checkable claim on the front and remove the rest

slides.notes: Hypothesis 01 gates the rest: a checkable claim on an uneven bottle invites the one-star review. Keep the gift box only once an entry pack exists, or trial disappears. Companion document, section 3.4 (H).

slides.title: Test five changes to TMC's packs: *thumbnail check, gift box apart* (2 of 2)

rows.label: Check every hero pack as a thumbnail
rows.sub: On a white background, before approving it

rows.label: Keep the gift box a separate product
rows.sub: For the gift buyer; do not let it define the daily pack

slides.notes: Companion document, section 3.4 (H).

title: Real price.
*One checkable claim.*
A pack that proves it.
slides.sub: TMC DOES NONE OF THE THREE YET
slides.notes: Source: 107 prices read 3 October 2026; brand pages; trade press (F).

slides.title: Three decisions for TMC

rows.label: One price for Black on every channel
rows.sub: Confirm the five prices on the live pages; fix one list and one selling price before any increase.

rows.label: Test two claim versions at the same price (H)
rows.sub: Rebuild the page on one checkable claim before the creative work starts.

rows.label: Put an entry pack under Rs 200 on the shelf (H)
rows.sub: The Rs 99 and Rs 199 minis are in TMC's v7 plan, not on the shelf (I).

slides.notes: Order: fix Black's content and spray first (pack hypothesis 01). All three build position A; B needs a named result TMC does not have yet. Size of prize: add Black's revenue and channel margin from Chapter A §2 before the meeting.

rows.sub: Nykaa August audit, Instagram counts, the TMC review analysis. (F) published, (E) estimate, (H) hypothesis to test.
